linear.text: Claim under test: V-POD-M+H2O2 reduces S. aureus and E. coli to zero colonies, where POD-M+H2O2 leaves 45-58 CFU
Read the panel: F5c [SEM]
Ruling: After H2O2 the POD-M octahedra are gone and only crumpled sheets remain, an alternative reason for the weak killing that the text never weig

traces.question: The claim above states that V-POD-M+H2O2 reduces S. aureus and E. coli to zero colonies while POD-M+H2O2 alone leaves 45-58 CFU. Looking at the SEM panel F5c, what does it show about the POD-M structure after H2O2 treatment that bears on why POD-M+H2O2 performs so much worse?
traces.answer_key: The panel shows that after H2O2 treatment the POD-M octahedra are gone and only crumpled sheets remain. This is an alternative reason for the weak killing by POD-M+H2O2 that the paper's text never weighs against its stated mechanism (a3).
traces.grading: Answer key: the audit ruling on the panel (a3), checked against the given claim s15 and panel F5c.

linear.text: Claim under test: Cu(II) and MoO3 together turn H2O2 into hydroxyl radicals far faster than either centre alone
Read the panel: F2f [PL]
Ruling: All four TA groups give 185-380 a.u. of TAOH fluorescence, so the Cu(II)+MoO3 gain is about twofold over the blank, not an on/off signal

traces.question: The claim under test says Cu(II) and MoO3 together convert H2O2 into hydroxyl radicals far faster than either centre alone. Does the PL panel (F2f), which compares TAOH fluorescence across the TA-only, Cu(II)-only, MoO3-only, and combined Cu(II)+MoO3 conditions, support this claim?
traces.answer_key: No. All four TA groups give 185-380 a.u. of TAOH fluorescence, so the Cu(II)+MoO3 condition shows only about a twofold gain over the blank rather than the dramatic, far-faster rate the claim implies -- it is not an on/off signal.

linear.text: Claim under test: MoO3 binds H2O2 into a peroxo-complex intermediate that lowers the Fenton-like barrier at Cu, accelerating .OH release
Read the panel: F2c [UVVIS]
Ruling: MoO3 alone gives absorbance 0.055 against 0.017 for H2O2 alone and 0.082 for Cu(II) alone, so MoO3 by itself does oxidize TMB

traces.question: The claim under test holds that MoO3 binds H2O2 into a peroxo-complex intermediate that only becomes catalytically active once paired with Cu, implying MoO3 by itself should barely touch TMB. Based on the TMB-oxidation comparison in panel F2c across the separate and combined MoO3/H2O2/Cu(II) conditions, does the panel support that exclusivity?
traces.answer_key: No. Panel F2c shows MoO3 alone already gives an absorbance of 0.055, versus 0.017 for H2O2 alone and 0.082 for Cu(II) alone. MoO3 by itself measurably oxidizes TMB, so it is not an inert partner that only turns active in combination with Cu; the panel qualifies the claim rather than confirming it (a1).
